# Current state — jpegxl-rs

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

_(none)_

## Constraints

### Correctness order: conformance before performance

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.correctness-before-speed/1` · scope `all` · topic `correctness-order`

Work proceeds in this order of priority: conformance, resource safety, memory
ownership, scalar performance, parallelism, SIMD, then encoder quality search.

### Correctness is measured by pixels, not byte-parity with libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.correctness-metrics/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/**"` · topic `correctness-metrics`

Decoder success is not lossless correctness. Conformance compares parse success,
dimensions, bit depth, color interpretation, frame count, an exact pixel hash for
lossless paths, and peak error plus RMSE for conforming lossy paths. Byte-for-byte
parity with libjxl is not a general target.

### The decoder enforces explicit resource limits

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.decoder-resource-limits/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `resource-limits`

The decoder enforces explicit, configurable upper bounds and validates all TOC
ranges before allocating or launching workers.

### Start forbidding unsafe; add SIMD unsafe only with a local contract

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.forbid-unsafe-by-default/1` · scope `all` · topic `unsafe-policy`

Crates start with forbid(unsafe_code). Unsafe SIMD is added only after profiles show
a concrete bottleneck and only where the safety contract is local and documented.

### No runtime dependency on libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.no-libjxl-runtime-dep/1` · scope `all` · topic `no-libjxl-dep`

The shipped library has no runtime dependency on libjxl or any C JPEG XL codec.
External decoders are invoked only as separate processes by the conformance harness.

### Parsers use checked arithmetic and never panic on bad input

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.no-panic-checked-arith/1` · scope `all` · topic `no-panic`

Every parser operation uses checked arithmetic and enforces resource limits.
Invalid or unsupported syntax returns a typed error; it never panics and never
silently substitutes defaults.

## Policies

### Clean-room: no architectural port of libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.clean-room-boundary/1` · scope `all` · topic `clean-room`

This is a native, standard-first Rust implementation. Implement from ISO/IEC 18181
and legitimately obtained specifications, never by porting libjxl architecture or
code. libjxl and other decoders are validation oracles only.

### Test count is not confidence; unknown coverage stays unknown

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.coverage-honesty/1` · scope `all` · topic `coverage-honesty`

Do not equate the number of tests with confidence, and do not claim conformance
coverage that has not been demonstrated against the corpus. Unknown profile and
feature coverage must be recorded as unknown, not assumed.

### E.4.4 ICC tag dictionary has 17 entries; use the LaTeX

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.e44-tag-dictionary/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `e44-tag-dictionary`

The E.4.4 tag dictionary has 17 entries (tagcode range 4..=20), including bTRC and
dmda. part1.md truncates it to 15 (OCR dropped those two). Use the LaTeX source;
confirmed by byte-exact fixtures.

### Encoder heuristics are not normative; keep them out of the syntax model

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.encoder-analysis-separate/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `encoder-analysis`

Keep encoder analysis (predictor evaluation, MA-tree construction, context
clustering, palette/RCT/Squeeze selection, LZ77 matching, block/quant search)
separate from the decoder-visible syntax model. A decoder-visible MaTree is
normative data; the algorithm that discovers it is not. Do not let an encoder
heuristic become a decoder requirement.

### EXPERIMENT_CLAMP_SYMMETRIC = false is not a loosened check

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.h52-clamp-asymmetric/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `h52-clamp`

Keep the asymmetric H.5.2 clamp (EXPERIMENT_CLAMP_SYMMETRIC = false). Do not
restore the printed symmetric clamp "to match the spec".

### jpxl bench isolates Modular and VarDCT encode paths

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.jpxl-bench-entry-points/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `jpxl-bench-entry-points`

Profile Modular and VarDCT separately. The CLI encode path is Modular only; a
flamegraph of jpxl encode does not describe VarDCT.

Measurement modes via release jpxl bench:
- modular: Modular lossless (MA search, residuals, LZ77, entropy, bit writing)
- vardct-fixed: VarDCT fixed quantizer (transform selection, transforms, CfL,
  quantize, emit; no rate-loop multiplication)
- vardct-rate: VarDCT target rate (full exact-price rate loop)
- vardct-probe: one predetermined quantizer plan+emit

Optional --input path.ppm (8-bit RGB P6) replaces the synthetic RGB pattern.
Output fields: wall_ms_total, wall_ms_median, output_bytes, and an FNV-1a
fingerprint for cross-iteration identity. Promote to a baseline only under
@jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules (crypto hashes of binary and stream,
decode gate, size classes); FNV alone is not enough for promotion.

### modular_16bit_buffers = false for >8-bit encodes is deliberate

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.modular-16bit-buffers/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `modular-16bit-buffers`

For >8-bit encodes, modular_16bit_buffers = false is deliberate: it is a truthful
claim about decoder working buffers (D.3), and its paired consequence is the jxll
level-10 box in container output (Annex M). Do not restore the Table D.3 default.

### Modular residual LZ77 must use H.3 dist_multiplier

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.modular-lz77-dist-multiplier/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"` · topic `modular-lz77-dist`

The residual SymbolDecoder must be given set_dist_multiplier(max_channel_width).
Encode distances as raw = distance + 119 when M > 0 (C.3.3 past the special table),
never raw = distance - 1 as if M = 0. Do not "fix" round-trip failures under full
modular decode by forcing M = 0 on the decoder.

### Correctness gates by optimization change type

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.optimization-correctness-gates/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"` · topic `optimization-gates`

Gate each optimization class before merge: bulk bit writer, plan Arc-sharing,
flat coefficient arena, and scratch reuse require byte-identical codestreams;
Rayon section encoding requires byte-identical results across thread counts;
integer SIMD requires scalar-versus-SIMD byte identity; floating DCT
factorization or SIMD requires decode validity plus the declared Contract A or
B; search pruning or approximate prices requires size/quality/target adherence
and an exact final-price gate; LZ77 algorithm changes require byte equality if
tie rules are preserved, otherwise equal or better exact stream size. Validate
with the in-project decoder and libjxl (oracle process). Decode time is not
included in encode timing.

### Pass oracle output format explicitly; do not loosen the PPM parser

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.oracle-output-format/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/**"` · topic `oracle-output-format`

jxl-oxide ignores the output-file extension and writes PNG bytes into any filename.
Pass --output-format explicitly. Do not "fix" a BadMagic PPM parse error by
loosening the PPM parser; the harness rejects PPM-from-jxl-oxide before spawning
(OracleError::UnsupportedFormat).

### Promoted performance baseline rules

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules/1` · scope `path "JPXL/**"` · topic `performance-baseline-rules`

A number is a promoted performance baseline only when all of the following hold;
otherwise it is a scratch or diagnostic measurement and must not be treated as a
baseline claim:

1. Immutable binaries: hash every binary involved; recheck before every timed run
   and reject the run if the hash changed.
2. Pinned inputs: exact image, its hash, dimensions, bit depth, and color encoding.
3. Interleaved A/B, never separate batches; report minimum, median, and dispersion.
4. Correctness gate alongside timing: output bytes and hash, and decoded-pixel
   result. A fast wrong answer is not a datum.
5. Host state: thread count, CPU affinity and policy, load, free memory, swap and
   tmpfs use, competing jobs. Measurements under resource pressure are diagnostics
   only, never baselines.
6. Cache regime stated: cold-cache, warm-cache, and warm-process are distinct;
   never merge them.
7. Size classes: at minimum a small (~4 MP) and a large (≥12 MP) image.
8. Unknown stays unknown: if profiling explains 48% of samples, report 48% and
   label the rest UNKNOWN.

Profile Modular and VarDCT separately. The CLI encode path is Modular-only; a
flamegraph of jpxl encode does not describe VarDCT. On hybrid Intel hosts, prefer
an explicit userspace P-core event (cpu_core/cycles/u) and verify that the folded
period total equals the perf event total before trusting an SVG.

### Prefer the LaTeX and image scans over OCR transcriptions

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.prefer-latex-over-ocr/1` · scope `all` · topic `source-of-truth`

For normative constants and algorithms, prefer the LaTeX transcription and, when in
doubt, the image scan, over OCR-derived markdown (part1.md and similar). Do not
re-transcribe values from a source already known to be corrupted; cite the verified
source in the record that carries the value.

### Keep research metrics and benchmarks out of the codec core

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.research-out-of-core/1` · scope `all` · topic `research-separation`

The codec core carries no research metrics, perceptual scoring, or benchmark
scaffolding (for example Butteraugli belongs to encoder development tooling, not the
decoder). The changelog is not a research database. Durable measurement summaries
and baseline rules live in AKR; full raw run logs and flamegraph artifacts live
under .agent/scratch/ (not pruned by akr build). Frozen experiment writeups may
go in JPXL/docs/experiments/ when a self-contained report is warranted.
JPXL/docs/PERFORMANCE.md is a stub only, not the measurement store.

### The encoder writes RestorationFilter explicitly OFF

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.restoration-filter-off/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `restoration-filter`

The encoder writes RestorationFilter explicitly OFF (gab = false, epf_iters = 0)
rather than relying on the Table J.1 defaults (gab = true, epf_iters = 2), because
those defaults are decoder-side smoothing our decoder does not implement yet. If
external decodes drift while self-roundtrip stays green, look here first.

### Retain external advice under sources/; mark completion in AKR

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.sources-advice-completion/1` · scope `all` · topic `sources-advice`

External architecture and optimization advice documents are retained under
the repository sources/ tree (for example sources/outside-advice.md) and
must not be deleted solely because their recommendations were adopted.
Progress against such a document is recorded only through AKR: propose or
revise work and milestones for each phase, attach evidence, and complete
those records when acceptance checks pass. Do not rewrite the advice
document into a checklist of strikethroughs or a second plan-of-record;
cite its path from AKR records instead.

### When every transcription agrees on nonsense, suspect the pipeline

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.suspect-transcription-pipeline/1` · scope `all` · topic `transcription-pipeline`

When every transcription agrees on nonsense, suspect the transcription pipeline,
not the standard. Escalate to the image scan before claiming a standard defect.

## Observations

### At matched bitrate our single-pass activity AQ field is a net perceptual loss: off beats every tuning tried, on both metrics

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.aq-field-is-a-net-perceptual-loss-2026-08-10/2`

The adaptive-quantization field, as tuned and as shipped, is a net PERCEPTUAL LOSS at matched bitrate. Turning it off improves both perceptual metrics.

Method: sweep the field's three constants at a FIXED bitrate and score each result with jpxl compare. Fixed-rate because AQ does not change how many bits are spent, only where, so the honest question is "at the same file size, which allocation looks better". Driver and raw output in .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/aq-sweep.ps1 and aq-sweep-0p8MP-{1,2}bpp.txt. `strength = 0` produces a neutral field, which AqSetup treats exactly as AqMode::Off, so that row IS "AQ disabled".

small_0p8MP at 1.0 bpp (bytes, ssimulacra2 higher-better, butteraugli lower-better):
AQ OFF (strength 0) -- 98141, 59.378, 6.075. Shipped (0.25/1.0/0.35) -- 97769, 59.617, 6.636.
Every other config tried: strength 0.10 (6.710), 0.40 (6.776), 0.60 (6.732), 1.00 (6.633); clamp 0.5 (6.781), 2.0 (6.583); chroma 0.0 (6.756), 1.0 (6.784).

small_0p8MP at 2.0 bpp:
AQ OFF -- 196459, 81.971, 3.185. Shipped -- 195444, 80.007, 3.562.
Every other config: ssimulacra2 79.64-80.01, butteraugli 3.447-3.828.

Two things stand out. First, AQ-off is not the end of a trend -- it is an OUTLIER. Every non-zero strength, every clamp and every chroma weight clusters tightly (butteraugli 6.58-6.78 at 1 bpp, 3.45-3.83 at 2 bpp) while AQ-off sits well outside it. So this is not "the strength constant is mistuned"; it is that having a non-neutral field at all costs perceptual quality here. Second, the penalty does not shrink as the rate rises -- at 2 bpp AQ-off is better on BOTH metrics (+1.96 ssimulacra2 and -10.6% butteraugli), where at 1 bpp it was better on butteraugli (-8.4%) and marginally worse on ssimulacra2. That rules out the obvious explanation of the per-varblock HfMul signalling row eating the coefficient budget, which would fade as a fraction of a larger file.

A likely reason it was never caught: M7's acceptance evidence (jpegxl-rs.evidence.m7-adaptive-quant) reads "spatial quality uniformity improved with stable target size". Uniformity is what AqMode::Uniform optimises -- busy atoms finer, error equalised. Production ships the opposite direction, AqMode::Masking (busy atoms coarser), whose case is perceptual masking and which the uniformity criterion does not test. So the shipped direction was accepted on a criterion the other direction satisfies, and no perceptual metric existed in this repository to check it against until now.

INTERPRETATION, sharpened by cross-project evidence (jpegxl-rs.observation.bpg-rs-aq-precedent-2026-08-10/2): this field is a SINGLE-PASS ACTIVITY field, and that is the class that also busted in bpg-rs, where two-pass measured AQ pays 3-10% but every single-pass mode did not. So the right reading is not "AQ does not pay here" but "this KIND of AQ does not pay here, and retuning its constants cannot fix it because the signal is the problem". NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and this should not become a default flip until it is: one image, two rates, one host. Untested are the other two corpus images, other rates, AqMode::Uniform (which would separate "this direction is wrong" from "the machinery costs quality regardless of direction"), and any non-photographic content, where masking is most likely to earn its keep. The measurement infrastructure to settle all of that now exists (EncodeRequest::budget.aq_tuning, `jpxl encode --aq-strength/--aq-clamp/--aq-chroma`, `jpxl compare --features perceptual`).

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.observation.aq-field-is-a-net-perceptual-loss-2026-08-10/1`

### AQ precedent from bpg-rs: two-pass measured AQ pays 3-10%; every single-pass activity mode busted -- and ours is single-pass

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.bpg-rs-aq-precedent-2026-08-10/2`

Cross-project precedent from the sibling still-image codec at D:\\Rust-projects\\bpg-rs (still265, HEVC lineage), on which kinds of adaptive quantization pay and which do not.

THE SPLIT THAT MATTERS: two-pass *measured* AQ works there -- 3-10% gains. Every single-pass mode was a bust. That distinction, not "AQ good/bad", is the transferable lesson.

Source note and a correction to an earlier draft of this record: an automated read of that repository's git history, docs and ledger found no committed number crediting AQ, and this record initially concluded there was no payoff. That was wrong. The two-pass result is known directly from the project's author; the harness (scripts/aq_experiment.py) writes bdrate_vs_uniform.csv / equal_byte_deltas.csv and those output files were never committed, which is why a repository-only read could not see them. Absence of a committed CSV is not absence of a result -- a reminder that a repo read is evidence about the repo, not about what was measured.

What busted there, and is visible in the history: the initial default-on per-CU variance AQ (commit d87aee7) was backed out a day later (6fc5dae) -- "the per-CU variance AQ on the speed tiers hurt quality and scrambled the ladder" -- and the same commit set AQ off by default. The docs record the single-pass activity attempts as "neutral-to-negative on photos" and "not the main photo-gap lever" (docs/ssimtune.md:325). The AqMode enum's other single-pass variants (LegacyShrink, Perceptual, PerceptualChroma, PsnrProbe, PositiveProbe) were likewise not adopted.

What works there: AqMode::TwoPassMeasured (commit fec6680). Pass 1 encodes and measures per-quantization-group *coded coefficient energy*; pass 2 redistributes QP from that measurement. An A/B over candidate signals -- coefficient energy vs rd(D+lambda R) vs SSE vs bits -- found coefficient energy "wins decisively". A three-pass candidate-compare gate gives it a safety property: it encodes a uniform-QP pass too, compares at equal bytes, and reverts to uniform when AQ would lose, so "two-pass AQ can improve a picture but never regress one".

Also on record there, unchanged by the correction: the "~3%" in commit 6fc5dae is the whole-encoder BD-rate gap against x265 m9, not an AQ figure, and that commit turned AQ off. Sign-data hiding was a separate, clean equal-bytes win (~+0.05 dB, 15-20% of the measured gap) and was promoted to default. AQ-active configs are forced out of the WPP parallel fast path, so AQ costs throughput as well as effort.

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE, and it is not what it first appeared. Our field (jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs) is a SINGLE-PASS ACTIVITY field: log2(1+variance) per 8x8 atom against the frame mean, luma plus down-weighted chroma, x265-family strength and clamp. That is precisely the class that busted in bpg-rs -- and jpegxl-rs.observation.aq-field-is-a-net-perceptual-loss-2026-08-10 independently measures ours to be neutral-to-negative on photos at matched bitrate, the same verdict. Two codecs, different transforms, different metrics, same result for the same class of method.

So the conclusion is NOT "AQ does not pay". It is: single-pass activity AQ does not pay, and no amount of retuning our three constants will change that, because the signal is the problem. If AQ is ever revisited here it should be built as two-pass measured -- measure coded coefficient energy per group in pass 1, redistribute in pass 2, and gate it against a uniform-QP encode at equal bytes so it cannot regress. That is a substantial build, it multiplies encode cost in a codec already 58-530x slower than cjxl, and it is explicitly deferred until the speed and rate-loop problems are fixed.

Scope limit: evidence about one other implementation's experience, and one of the numbers in it is reported rather than read from a file.

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.observation.bpg-rs-aq-precedent-2026-08-10/1`

### Head-to-head vs cjxl 0.13: jpxl is at cjxl -e1 density, 5-24x slower, and its effort ladder is inert above level 1

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.libjxl-headsup-modular-2026-08-10/1`

Head-to-head against the libjxl oracle on the three-image real-photo corpus (.agent/scratch/realworld-bench-20260806T072202Z), lossless modular, both codecs at their default thread counts, on this Windows host. jpxl at effort 1/3/5/7/9 versus cjxl v0.13.0 (196a43d9, MinGW, AVX2) at -d 0 -e 1..9. Bytes and wall milliseconds:

small_0p8MP (1024x768): jpxl e1 1,075,465 @ 295ms; e3/e5/e7 identical bytes @ 649/837/1320ms; e9 1,037,868 @ 10,291ms. cjxl e1 1,082,673 @ 61ms; e3 890,029 @ 44ms; e7 873,503 @ 144ms; e9 866,855 @ 597ms.

mid_4MP (2400x1800): jpxl e1 5,157,974 @ 521ms; e3/e5/e7 identical @ 2258/3320/5680ms; e9 4,942,547 @ 55,156ms. cjxl e1 5,414,251 @ 33ms; e3 4,273,458 @ 139ms; e7 4,097,956 @ 520ms; e9 4,054,479 @ 2301ms.

large_12MP (4000x3000): jpxl e1 through e9 ALL emit 9,795,599 bytes, at 1272/6118/9774/18,200/65,437ms. cjxl e1 9,870,951 @ 54ms; e5 7,646,073 @ 632ms; e7 6,921,886 @ 1147ms; e9 6,756,132 @ 6825ms.

Three things follow. (1) Density: jpxl sits at roughly cjxl -e1, beating it by 0.8-4.7% on bytes, and is 20-31% larger than cjxl -e7 (12MP: 9,795,599 vs 6,921,886, +41.5% bytes for the same 1.1-1.3s of wall time). (2) Speed: jpxl -e1 is 5x slower than cjxl -e1 at 0.8MP, 16x at 4MP, 24x at 12MP -- the gap widens with size, so it is throughput, not fixed overhead. (3) The effort ladder is nearly inert: at 12MP levels 1 through 9 emit byte-identical output for 51x the wall time, and at the smaller sizes only level 9 moves at all (-3.5% / -4.2%) at 35x / 106x the time of level 1.

The mechanism behind (3) is visible in the code, not just the numbers: plan_for caps the tree at 2 leaves / depth 1 whenever the frame exceeds deep_search_sample_cap, whose largest value is 1<<18 = 262,144 samples at effort 9. Every image in this corpus, including the smallest at 786,432 samples, exceeds that cap, so no level ever searches a tree deeper than one binary split. The density levers the higher band would need -- many-context MA trees, RCT type selection (the encoder hardcodes YCoCg; H.6.3 defines 42 types), and LZ77 inside the cost model (already scoped as Phase 4D) -- are not reachable from the current ladder at any real image size.

How it was measured: a PowerShell driver (preserved at .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/headsup.ps1, raw output alongside it in headsup-2026-08-10.txt) times one encode per (image, codec, setting) with Diagnostics.Stopwatch around the process invocation and reads the output length from the file system. jpxl is invoked as `jpxl encode <ppm> <out> --effort N`; cjxl as `cjxl <ppm> <out> -d 0 -e N`, using the pinned Windows oracle build in JPXL/tools/oracle-bin (cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9, AVX2, per PINNED_REVISIONS.txt). Both codecs run at their own default thread count, so these are end-to-end wall times as a user would see them, not per-core algorithmic cost.

Scope limit: three photographs on one host, one timed run per cell, no warm-up. It is a direction-setting measurement, not a promoted baseline; the timings are not medians and should not be quoted as such.

### Lossy RD on three metrics: 12-20% behind cjxl on SSIMULACRA2 but 39-53% on butteraugli, localising the deficit to perceptual bit allocation

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-perceptual-baseline-2026-08-10/1`

Rate/distortion baseline for the lossy VarDCT path against cjxl v0.13.0, scored on three metrics: PSNR (signal error), SSIMULACRA2 (perceptual, higher better, 100 = identical) and butteraugli distance (perceptual, LOWER better, and the metric cjxl -d actually optimises). Corpus: the three real photographs in .agent/scratch/realworld-bench-20260806T072202Z. JPXL swept by --bpp, cjxl by -d, cjxl output decoded with the oracle's own djxl. Full 24-cell table in .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/headsup-lossy-perceptual-baseline.txt.

THE HEADLINE: the size of the gap depends on which metric you ask, by a factor of three, and the two readings say different things.

Comparing at EQUAL QUALITY (interpolating cjxl's curve to jpxl's operating point), cjxl's bitrate saving is:

SSIMULACRA2 -- 0.8 MP ~17% (jpxl 80.0 at 1.988 bpp vs cjxl ~1.66), 4 MP ~12% (jpxl 85.3 at 1.996 vs cjxl ~1.76), 12 MP ~20% (jpxl 87.9 at 1.673 vs cjxl ~1.34).
PSNR -- 0.8 MP ~26%, 4 MP ~25%, 12 MP ~37%.
Butteraugli -- 0.8 MP ~43% (jpxl 3.56 at 1.988 bpp vs cjxl ~1.13), 4 MP ~39% (jpxl 2.01 at 1.996 vs cjxl ~1.21), 12 MP ~53% (jpxl 1.96 at 1.673 vs cjxl ~0.79).

Two conclusions follow, and they are not the same conclusion.

(1) On SSIMULACRA2 the codec is within 12-20% of cjxl. That is a much smaller deficit than the PSNR-only reading in jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-vardct-headsup-2026-08-10 suggested, and it says the transform, quantization and entropy layers are fundamentally sound -- this is not an encoder that is broadly behind.

(2) On butteraugli the deficit is 39-53%, three to four times the SSIMULACRA2 figure. Butteraugli is what cjxl tunes for, so some of that is expected; but a gap that much larger on one perceptual metric than another localises the deficit to PERCEPTUAL BIT ALLOCATION -- where bits go within a frame -- rather than to coding efficiency, which both metrics would punish equally. Concretely that points at the adaptive-quantization field (jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs), whose three constants (AQ_STRENGTH 0.25, AQ_CLAMP 1.0, CHROMA_AQ_WEIGHT 0.35) came from the 8-bit x265-family literature and had never been validated against any perceptual metric on this codec's output, because until this session the repository had none.

Speed, unchanged from the earlier PSNR-only run and still the largest practical gap: jpxl is 58-530x slower at every size and rate (8.7-71 s vs 0.09-0.20 s at 0.8 MP; 63-687 s vs 0.75-1.62 s at 12 MP).

Scope limit: three photographs, one host, one timed run per cell. The equal-quality bitrates are interpolated between adjacent cjxl rungs, not measured directly, so treat them as approximate. Direction-setting, not a promoted baseline. PSNR and SSIMULACRA2 and butteraugli disagree here by design -- do not quote one of them as "the" gap.

### Lossy VarDCT vs cjxl (PSNR-only, superseded as a summary): 58-530x slower; high-rate miss traced to LF-fill ordering at adjacent rungs

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-vardct-headsup-2026-08-10/3`

First rate/distortion comparison of the lossy VarDCT path against the oracle. Corpus: the three real photographs in .agent/scratch/realworld-bench-20260806T072202Z. JPXL swept by --bpp, cjxl v0.13.0 swept by -d, cjxl output decoded with the oracle's own djxl so a JPXL decode bug cannot masquerade as a cjxl quality difference. Raw original rows: .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/headsup-lossy-2026-08-10.txt.

SCOPE CORRECTION (revision 2, retained): this record measured PSNR only. jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-perceptual-baseline-2026-08-10 re-measures SSIMULACRA2 and butteraugli and finds a 12-20% gap on one and 39-53% on the other. The original density result is only the PSNR gap.

Measured original (bpp, PSNR dB, encode ms): 0.8 MP -- jpxl (0.499,24.94,8724) (0.995,28.72,17602) (1.988,34.04,34973) (3.999,41.56,55646); cjxl (0.839,30.55,154) (1.466,34.22,94) (2.321,37.91,106) (3.428,41.00,104). 4 MP -- jpxl (0.498,27.47,38076) (0.995,32.64,55376) (1.996,37.40,106791) (3.645,41.62,178646); cjxl (0.565,32.27,551) (0.941,35.15,336) (1.490,37.78,341) (2.366,40.18,309). 12 MP -- jpxl (0.499,31.67,63214) (0.997,36.67,144969) (1.673,39.32,472352) (3.942,45.72,462885); cjxl (0.414,34.83,1534) (0.677,37.18,944) (1.074,39.54,897) (1.765,42.18,754).

(1) On PSNR, cjxl reaches equal PSNR at roughly 25-37% fewer bits. Superseded as a general quality summary by the perceptual record above. (2) Speed: jpxl was 58-530x slower because a targeted encode prices 15-40 full-frame plans; this remains the largest practical gap.

(3) HIGH-RATE UNDERSHOOT -- CAUSE CORRECTED AGAIN IN REVISION 3. Revision 1 incorrectly called it a ladder ceiling. Revision 2 correctly rejected that but then inferred from `24 fast` that bracketing/bisection exhausted the Fast cap. Phase 4M's new phase/rung telemetry shows that inference was also wrong.

At 0.8 MP / 4 bpp, the 20 Fast prices split into 3 Bracket + 7 Bisect + 2 Fill + 8 LF-fill; Fast best/upper were adjacent rungs 73728/73729 and Full started/ended at 73728. At 4 MP / 4 bpp, 24 Fast split into 3 Bracket + 14 Bisect + 3 Fill + 4 LF-fill; Fast best/upper were adjacent 73729/73730 and Full started/ended at 73729. The ladder had settled; the aggregate count included secondary LF probes.

The actual narrow defect was LF-fill order. With requested quant_lf=16 and only four remaining slots, absolute-distance order tried 12, 8, 24, 32. The first two make LF coarser while trying to spend an undershoot. Finer-only order reached 24, 32, 48, 64; exact pricing selected 64 and raised the 4 MP result from 1,954,100 to 2,003,736 bytes, reducing the miss from about 9.5% to 7.2%, for about a 2% single-run diagnostic wall increase. Lower-rate 0.8 MP outputs stayed byte-identical. Raw Phase 4M summary: .agent/scratch/phase4m-lf-fill-direction-2026-08-11.md.

The remaining 4 MP miss is not attributed here beyond the measured trace; the 12 MP / 2 bpp case has not yet been re-run with phase telemetry and remains unknown. Do not restore either the ladder-ceiling or generic Fast-bracketing-exhaustion diagnosis.

### Retiring the tree-depth cap changes nothing; the cheap ranker's unit mismatch was the inertness

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.modular-depth-is-not-the-lever-2026-08-10/1`

MA-tree depth is not what the modular effort ladder was missing. The cheap ranker's unit mismatch was.

The deep_search_sample_cap was believed to be the blocker: it collapses the tree to max_leaves=2, max_depth=1 whenever a frame exceeds it, and its largest value (1<<18) is below every real photograph, so no effort level ever searched past one binary split. Retiring it changes nothing. With `--modular-deep-cap full` on the 4 MP corpus image, efforts 7, 8 and 9 all converge on the SAME output -- 4,942,547 bytes, fingerprint 771811b28ce7ab6e -- as they do with the cap in place. Depth beyond one split, and the finer THRESH_FINE grid that efforts 8-9 add, buy exactly zero bytes. The greedy split loop stops improving after its first round regardless of how much depth it is allowed.

What was actually wrong is a units error in lossless::total_cost_source: it added an unscaled whole-frame `ma_tree_bit_cost * sections` to a residual estimate covering only 1/row_stride of the frame. A split's saving was therefore divided by the stride while its cost was not, over-pricing every extra context by exactly the sampling ratio -- and the ratio grows with frame size, which is why the ladder looked progressively more inert on bigger images. Measured proof of the mechanism before the fix, on the 4 MP image: at stride 1 (effort 9) the winning split IS found (4,942,547 B); at stride 4 (effort 7) the same split is rejected (5,157,974 B). Same content, same candidate, different verdict purely from the sampling ratio.

With estimate_residual_bits_sampled extrapolating to whole-frame bits, effort 7 finds at stride 4 the tree that previously only stride 1 could reach: 0.8 MP 1,075,465 -> 1,037,868 B (-3.5%), 4 MP 5,157,974 -> 4,942,547 B (-4.2%), 12 MP unchanged at 9,795,599 B (no split wins there at any stride, before or after). Against cjxl -e7 the 4 MP gap narrows from +25.9% to +20.6% -- real, and nowhere near closed.

Two consequences worth acting on. (1) Effort 7's output is no longer byte-identical to the pre-effort-ramp encoder; that anchor property was retired deliberately and the corpus gate now pins the default (effort 1), which short-circuits the search entirely and is untouched. (2) Effort 7's wall time at 4 MP rose from ~5.7 s to ~47-50 s for the same ~71 residual scans, because the tree that now wins contains the Weighted (H.5) predictor, and estimate_residual_bits_sampled must fall back to a full sequential scan for any Weighted-containing tree -- so once Weighted wins the sweep, every one of the 56 split candidates carrying it forward becomes a full-frame scan. Bounding that is the obvious next target: score split TOPOLOGY with a stateless proxy and restore Weighted only in per-leaf refinement.

Scope limit: three photographs, one host, single runs. Direction-setting, not a promoted baseline.

## Assessments

### Architecture diagnosis: choose multiplicity and modular rescans (outside-advice)

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.encoder-architecture-outside-advice/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`, `path "sources/outside-advice.md"`

External review in sources/outside-advice.md (2026-08-06) diagnoses the
~15x VarDCT and ~30-100x Modular gaps versus libjxl as structural, not
leaf-SIMD deficits. VarDCT: EncodeRequest::defaults for bench_vardct_fixed
still runs hierarchical cover, AQ, CfL, and full entropy search; scalar
HfQuantizer::choose is invoked on the order of 10^8 calls at 12 MP
(cover scoring + CfL samples + factor trials + final quant); planning is
serial while rayon only parallelizes emission. Modular: plan_for rescans
residuals ~67-72 times and deep-clones planes each trial (~10 GB traffic
at 12 MP RGB) while producing e1-class density. Recommended order is
Phase 0 instrumentation, Phase 1 output-preserving fixes, then replace
quant/CfL/cover units of work, modular planner, perceptual calibration,
and only then entropy/SIMD/LTO. Rankings are source findings pending
Phase-0 measured counters.

### Encoder static assessment: multiplicity and structure before SIMD

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.encoder-static-optimization/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`

Static review of the encoder (no measured flamegraph on this snapshot) ranks
gains as: (1) bulk BitWriter instead of bit-at-a-time; (2) stop deep-cloning
quantized VarDCT plans; (3) cut rate-loop work that re-plans nearly everything
per probe; (4) factored scalar DCT32 before vectorizing the dense matrix path;
(5) group coefficient arenas instead of per-varblock heap; (6) cache selected
transforms within one probe; (7) tiered Modular MA/residual scoring instead of
exact-encoding dozens of candidates; (8) shape scalar loops for the compiler
before manual SIMD. Profile Modular, VarDCT fixed-quantizer, and VarDCT
target-rate separately. Rankings are source findings, not measured percentages.

### Modular full search is chaff on real content; the lean config should be the default

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.modular-effort-lean-default/1`

On real photographic and smooth content the full modular search earns zero bytes over a single-predictor, single-leaf, collapsed search, while costing ~16x the wall time. Measured at 12MP (jpxl bench modular --diag): effort 1 does 1 residual scan, effort 7 does 71, and both emit the identical fingerprint dc380915d983b360 / 9,795,599 bytes. A content sweep (.agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10) shows effort 1 within 0% of best on photos and gradients, ~3.7% on a flat-block screenshot, at 5-17x the speed.

Per the bpg-rs precedent (commit 4e68042 'effort-tier restructuring': three canonical presets with explicit pipeline policies, the expensive tier kept cheap where it does not help), the expensive machinery (Weighted full-scans, the 56-candidate split grid, per-leaf refinement, finer stride, palette/squeeze trials) should be demoted to opt-in rather than remaining a tax on the default path. It is deliberately NOT deleted: those methods are load-bearing on content the synthetic fixtures do not represent (real UI/line-art -> palette; textured/noisy -> Weighted), and proving a method universally dead needs a broader real-world corpus.

Prose citations (V-005: an assessment cannot target a work record via supported_by): the implementing work is jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4e-modular-effort-ramp; the measurement evidence is jpegxl-rs.evidence.modular-search-chaff-2026-08-10 and jpegxl-rs.evidence.modular-effort-ramp-landed-2026-08-10.

### Correction: the '118x' figure is a wall-time ratio, not a density gap; jpxl-modular already beats cjxl -e1 on bytes

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-density-gap-is-vs-e7-only/1`

jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-order-correction (this session, prior revision) and the original jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped scoping both read the source claim '~118x slower than cjxl e1 for essentially identical output size' as evidence of a density/model-strength gap, and used that to justify front-loading 4A (Weighted predictor) and 4C (global tree) -- both density levers -- ahead of 4B (sampled property-gather, a search-time lever). The 4.0b density + decode-validity gate (jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4-0b-density-gate-2026-08-08, real corpus, current binary, decode-validated through both jpxl-decode and djxl) shows this reading was wrong: '118x slower... for essentially identical output size' means exactly what it says -- 118x is a TIME ratio (confirmed: 37.97s jpxl vs 0.317s cjxl -e1 at 12MP = 120x), and 'essentially identical output size' is accurate, not a euphemism for 'much larger.' Measured size ratios: jpxl-modular is 5-8% SMALLER than cjxl -e1 at every size class (0.944/0.953/0.992 across 0.8/4/12MP). There is no density gap versus cjxl -e1 -- jpxl already wins there. The real density gap is versus cjxl -e7 (max-effort search) only: jpxl trails by 16-42%, growing with image size (1.157/1.259/1.415).

This reverses the priority ordering. Modular's dominant, unambiguous problem is wall-clock cost (100-120x), driven by the 67 full-plane cheap-tier residual scans per plan_for call (lossless.rs:154-248) that 4B (sampled property-gather) directly targets. The density gap that does exist (vs e7 only, not e1) is smaller in relative terms (16-42% vs 100-120x) and is what 4A (Weighted predictor) and 4C (global tree) would address. Corrected sub-phase order: 4.0 (done) -> 4.0b (done) -> 4B -> 4A -> 4C -> 4D (optional tail, per the earlier not-on-hot-path finding which still holds).

4B remains the higher-implementation-risk item (proving sampled winner-selection matches full-scan selection, the 'invasive piece' per the original scoping) but is now also the higher-payoff item, reversing the earlier trade-off that ranked 4A/4C first partly because they looked cheaper AND more impactful. 4A is still cheap to build (mirrors jpxl-decode/src/modular/weighted.rs) and can run opportunistically alongside 4B design work if convenient, but should not block 4B on the critical path.

See also (prose citation, assessment cannot target work via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped, jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-order-correction, jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4-0b-density-gate-2026-08-08, jpegxl-rs.evidence.s8-phase-d-diagnostics-gated-verified.

### Advisor correction: Phase 4 order is 4.0b density-gate -> 4A -> 4C -> 4B -> 4D(optional), not 4A+4D-first

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-order-correction/1`

An independent Opus advisor review of jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped, run against live code (not the prior scoping summary), verified all four cited code facts (PREDICTOR_CANDIDATES omits Weighted at lossless.rs:70-78; use_global_tree hardcoded false at modular/mod.rs:1094; full-plane cheap scans at lossless.rs:154-241; 256-entry linear LZ77 lookback at modular/mod.rs:651,1499-1519) but surfaced two findings that overturn the proposed sub-phase order.

Finding A -- 4D (LZ77 hash-chain) is not on the wall-time hot path. greedy_lz77_events is reached only via encode_ans_stream_lz77, called from the Exact price tier and final emit (modular/mod.rs:1291-1295), not the cheap-tier scan loop. The session's own --diag run confirms the call-count split: exact_prices=3 vs cheap_scores=67 per plan_for call, flat across 256/1024/2048px sizes (topology-driven, not size-driven). The 33.5s modular wall is dominated by the 67 full-plane cheap residual scans (6 predictors x greedy split grid over SPLIT_PROPERTIES x SPLIT_THRESHOLDS + per-leaf refinement, lossless.rs:154-248), not LZ77 search cost. 4D is a modest density lever at best (helps only where a copy is already adopted, C.3.3 gate at modular/mod.rs:1361) and moves neither the wall-time nor the 118x density number materially -- demoted to an optional tail item.

Finding B -- 4A (Weighted/H.5 predictor) is far cheaper than scoped. The decoder already has a complete, tested clean-room implementation: crates/jpxl-decode/src/modular/weighted.rs (WeightedState::predict/update, max_error as property 15), invoked per-sample at jpxl-decode/src/modular/mod.rs:684-710. 4A is not "invent H.5," it is "mirror the decoder's working state machine on the encode residual path": add Predictor::Weighted=6 (must match decoder's enum index) and add property 15 to SPLIT_PROPERTIES (currently [4,5,6,7,9,10,11] at lossless.rs:81, missing 15). The only correctness hazard is byte-exact wrap/narrow arithmetic parity with the decoder (jpxl-decode/mod.rs:706-710) -- caught by the existing round-trip gate.

Corrected order: 4.0 (done, this session -- diag re-confirms 2026-08-06 numbers, no regression from S8-era VarDCT-only changes) -> 4.0b (NEW, zero-risk: pinned real-corpus density + decode-validity gate, see jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-0b-density-gate) -> 4A -> 4C -> 4B -> 4D (optional tail).

Rationale for reordering ahead of 4B: the project's optimization-determinism-contract requires Contract-B changes (deliberately altering encoder decisions -- 4A and 4C both do) to name metric bounds in an explicit revise; bounds cannot be named without a working density-measurement harness, which does not yet exist (jpxl-conformance/src/metrics.rs has pixel-error helpers only, no bpp/size-ratio helper). 4B (sampled property-gather) is a pure search-speed optimization -- the existing exact final-price gate (lossless.rs:259-306, PriceTier::Exact) already guarantees the emitted bytes are exactly priced regardless of how the search reached that candidate, so 4B does not block on density measurement and can follow once 4A/4C establish whether the model-strength gap is the real remaining cost.

See also (prior scoping context, cited in prose since assessment cannot target work records via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped, jpegxl-rs.assessment.s8-close-phase4-reorient, jpegxl-rs.assessment.encoder-architecture-outside-advice (source of the original, not-yet-refreshed-on-real-corpus 118x density claim that 4.0b exists to make live and reproducible).

### Advisor design: wire Weighted via sweep+refinement only, sequential collector, no property-15 split, four-part correctness gate

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4a-weighted-integration-design/1`

An independent Opus advisor review of jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4a-weighted-predictor-scoped (run against live code) gave an actionable design, subsequently implemented and verified (jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-weighted-predictor-wired-2026-08-08).

1. Placement: Weighted enters only via the single-leaf predictor sweep and per-leaf refinement (both already loop over PREDICTOR_CANDIDATES), NOT the greedy split search's inner loop. split_leaf always carries the parent leaf's chosen predictor forward unchanged ('same predictor both sides first'), so a Weighted-winning sweep result propagates into splits for free without the split loop needing its own Weighted branch.

2. Cost bound (advisor corrected the original framing): pricing any Weighted-containing tree requires a full sequential O(pixels) scan (sampling would desync the H.5 error state; the specialised single-leaf fast paths don't apply either). If Weighted wins the sweep, EVERY split-round candidate becomes Weighted-on-both-sides, meaning up to rounds x leaves x |SPLIT_PROPERTIES| x |SPLIT_THRESHOLDS| sequential scans, not the '1 + num_leaves' bound the original scoping assumed -- bounded in practice by DEEP_SEARCH_SAMPLE_CAP (large frames cap to one split round). Recommended measuring wall-time impact before committing further; not yet done as a formal A/B in this pass (deferred -- see note below).

3. Property 15 (max_error): deliberately excluded from SPLIT_PROPERTIES for this sub-phase. Confirmed a pure encoder-side search-cost decision with zero effect on decode behaviour or bitstream legality -- the decoder always runs WeightedState unconditionally regardless of what the encoder's search considers, and WPHeader is unconditionally present in every sub-bitstream per H.2 regardless of whether predictor 6 is used anywhere.

4. Correctness gate: sharing jpxl_core::modular_weighted makes the H.5.2 arithmetic question vacuous (same code both sides), but call-site parity (how each crate builds SelfCorrectingNeighbours, and whether the state advances correctly on every sample including non-Weighted-leaf samples in a mixed tree) is NOT vacuous and is the live risk. Gate implemented: forced single-leaf and mixed-tree round trips through jpxl-decode, an independent djxl oracle round trip (catches shared-module-vs-spec bugs a same-crate round trip cannot), and a multi-section round trip verifying WeightedState resets at group boundaries (all passing).

Deferred from this pass, per advisor's own conditional recommendation ('implement the simple version... run the gate, add mitigation only if the time gate trips'): the formal 2x/3x wall-time A/B gate and the surrogate-seeded topology mitigation. Implementation landed with correctness fully gated; the performance-regression risk flagged in point 2 above is a known open item, not yet measured on a large-frame Weighted-seeded corpus case.

See also (prose citation, assessment cannot target work via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4a-weighted-predictor-scoped, jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-weighted-predictor-wired-2026-08-08.

### Advisor reorientation: S8 closes as honest negative; Phase F no-go; next round is Phase 4 (modular, density-first)

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.s8-close-phase4-reorient/1`

Independent Opus-advisor review, checked against the actual code and AKR ledger rather than accepted at face value, on the question of where encoder optimization work should go after S8's closure.

Verification of the S8 closure holds up: the s8-cover-prune Cargo feature is confirmed not in default; cheap_stage_would_prune and all its call sites in lib.rs are #[cfg(feature = "s8-cover-prune")]; the measured net slowdown (+20-25% cover_ms) is consistent with cell_lower_bound's scalar loop losing to choose_lane4's SIMD batching. No Phase 4/5/6 AKR work items exist yet -- confirmed greenfield at the ledger level.

Correction to the pre-review framing: outside-advice.md §14's modular diagnosis is partly stale. Phase 1 (not just VarDCT-focused work) already fixed modular's cheapest problems -- plane deep-clones eliminated via Arc<[i32]> score-plane sharing (lossless.rs, ~10GiB->432MB at 12MP, wall ~44s->33.5s, byte-identical), specialized single-leaf residual kernels (modular/mod.rs West/North/Gradient fast paths), and cheap-vs-exact trial pricing (PriceTier::Cheap for search, PriceTier::Exact only on settled finalists). What remains from §14-15 is model-strength, not raw copy/interpretation cost: no Weighted predictor (lossless.rs, deferred), local-only MA trees (use_global_tree=false, no global histogram clustering), full-image cheap-tier trial scans (no sampled/summarized gather per §15), and a naive 256-entry linear LZ77 lookback with no cheap repetition gate.

A second correction: post-Phase-1-3, VarDCT's fattest 12MP stage is now entropy (3.68s of 8.3s total) not cover (1.79s) -- relevant to ruling out Phase F, since even a working within-probe cover prune would only target a ceiling of ~3% of VarDCT wall.

Phase F (S8's aggressive closed-form/continuous rate-estimate half) verdict: FIRM NO-GO. Four independent reasons: its own within-probe predecessor (Phase D) measured a net loss; the realistic ceiling is now tiny given entropy is the fat stage; CfL's closed-form-from-sufficient-statistics estimate was already tried and reverted twice at a smaller, safer decision surface (see phase2-cfl-quant evidence); and cover selection is a larger, more consequential surface where the same failure mode is more likely, not less.

Next-round recommendation: Phase 4 (rebuild modular planning), reframed density-first rather than a from-scratch rebuild, since the cheap speed wins are already banked by Phase 1. Justification: modular is the largest remaining absolute cost (33.5s vs VarDCT's 8.3s at 12MP, ~4x), the least-addressed gap proportionally (~22% wall reduction from one phase vs VarDCT's ~45% from three), has the worst density benchmark point on record (~118x slower at e1 for essentially identical output size -- a model-strength failure, not a speed one), and is the safest major rebuild available in this codebase because lossless gives an exact-pixel-identity oracle for every sub-phase with no Butteraugli/perceptual-calibration dependency (unlike further VarDCT work, which needs Phase 5 first). Phase 6 (entropy, the fattest VarDCT stage) is the strongest VarDCT-side alternative but outside-advice.md §20 deliberately orders low-level entropy work last, after architecture reshaping; Phase 5 (perceptual parity) is a prerequisite for judging VarDCT density honestly but is calibration-heavy and blocked on a §19 corpus with provenance sidecars that doesn't exist yet (test-set/ still violates AGENTS.md §9, tracked at S8's deferred Phase E).

Scoping sketch handed to jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped follows the same measure-before-design, prove-safety-before-wiring, honest-negatives-acceptable discipline S8 and phases 1-3 used: 4.0 re-measure the current (post-Phase-1) modular baseline by stage so no sub-phase re-solves what Phase 1 already fixed; 4A Weighted predictor (density, exact-lossless-safe -- byte size is the only oracle needed since lossless can't be "wrong", only bigger); 4D LZ77 gating via a cheap repetition estimate ahead of the full alternative encode (speed, output-preserving, byte-identity gate); 4B sampled property-gather replacing full-image cheap-tier trial scans (the invasive piece -- proven against the full-scan scorer on fixtures before wiring, same discipline as S8's regret-harness pattern, honest-negative-acceptable if winner selection drifts too far); 4C global/chunk-global tree + histogram clustering (density, interacts with the entropy stage so scoped separately). Suggested order 4.0 -> (4A + 4D) -> 4B -> 4C, front-loading the cheap/safe wins.

See also (precedent/context, cited in prose since assessment cannot target work records via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-s8-full-redesign-scoped (the closed S8 line this reorients from), jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase3-forward-cache (established the 96-97% cross-probe forward reuse this builds on), jpegxl-rs.observation.preopt-flamegraphs-2026-08-06 (pre-opt baseline flamegraphs).

### Closed-form HF CfL factor selection from 3 sufficient stats regressed correctness twice; reverted to exact-oracle scoring over a narrower window

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase2-analytic-cfl-regressed-correctness/1`

Two independent attempts to fully eliminate choose_cfl_y/choose_cfl_factor (superseding jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase2-cfl-choose-collapse) each regressed a real test when the HF CfL factor was decided from CflAccumulator's 3 sufficient statistics (s_yy, s_yc, s_cc) alone, without any per-sample exact scoring: (1) an invented Shannon-style rate proxy (variance vs. a representative quantization step, priced against factor_bits signaling cost) caused refine_hf_factor to pick the neutral factor for the "rgb-64x64" vardct_oracle fixture where the exact per-sample search picks non-neutral, failing that fixture's own precondition assertion ("the oracle fixture must put non-neutral CfL on the wire") in jxl_oxide_decodes_our_vardct_output. (2) Trusting CflAccumulator::best_factor's closed-form seed directly (no rate gate at all) passed that oracle fixture but then picked a non-neutral factor that cost more bytes than neutral for equal-or-better quality, failing jpxl-encode-policy::tests::cfl_reduces_size_at_equal_quality_on_correlated_colour (CfL 3647 B vs neutral 3493 B). Conclusion: 3 second-moment sufficient statistics are not enough information to reproduce the exact search's rate/distortion tradeoff at the tile level; a safe closed-form replacement needs either per-sample histogram-ish statistics or a properly calibrated rate model built against the matched-quality harness outside-advice.md §19 describes (jpegxl-rs.decision.encoder-architecture-phases already gates that behind Phase 2, but it turns out Phase 2's own HF factor step needs it too). Both attempts were reverted; the landed diff keeps only the already-safe factor_candidates window narrowing (±4 -> ±1) plus the seed==0 exact-LS-neutral shortcut, which are output-preserving-in-spirit (still exact-oracle-scored, just over fewer candidates) and independently verified: choose_total 285,647,118 -> 175,406,647 (-39%), choose_cfl_factor 154,335,540 -> 44,095,069 (-71%), choose_cfl_y unchanged at 11,812,500 (still exact, still needed by the retained per-sample scoring), all lib tests and (modulo the pre-existing, unrelated both_oracles_decode_a_stream_from_the_hf_mul_segment failure reproduced on unmodified f73590d) the oracle suite green.

### Rate-loop CandidateForwardCache cross-probe hit rate measured at ~96-97%; size cap not viable

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase3-rate-loop-cache-reuse-measured/1`

Extended `jpxl bench vardct-rate --diag` to print a new rate_diag= line (fast_prices, full_prices, dct_cache_hits/misses/hit_rate from RateOutcome.stats, which already existed but was never surfaced -- previously only the last probe's per-plan_at diag= line printed, hiding cross-probe reuse entirely). Measured CandidateForwardCache's actual cross-probe hit rate on two images: 12MP (4000x3000) at bpp=1.0 ran 23 total probes (11 fast + 12 full) with 6,349,453 hits vs 245,575 misses = 96.28% hit rate; misses (245,575) closely match the ~245,228 unique candidates a single vardct-fixed probe computes, confirming every probe after the first is scoring the *same* candidate set (position+transform doesn't depend on quantizer scale, only block_cost's score of each does) and getting a near-total cache hit. 1024x768 at bpp=1.0 ran 25 probes (13+12), 497,050 hits vs 16,127 misses = 96.86% hit rate -- same pattern, size-independent. Conclusion: cross-probe reuse is real, large (~20-25x effective multiplier on forward-DCT work across a default-budget rate search), and a size-capped/evicting cache would have to retain essentially 100% of one frame's unique candidates to preserve it -- a cap cannot meaningfully shrink CandidateForwardCache's memory footprint without directly costing proportional wall-time (up to ~23x more forward-DCT recomputation for evicted-then-needed entries). This closes the "measure-then-cap" option from jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase3-forward-cache's note: it is not viable at this frame's candidate-set scale. The remaining path to outside-advice.md §7's ~428 MB reduction is §8's compact-per-candidate-summary redesign (score from summaries, materialize full coefficients only for the winner), which is a larger, separately-scoped change touching block_cost/tile_region's candidate representation, not an isolated cache-policy tweak.

### Phase 4A: Weighted predictor wired into encoder search, decode-validated (jpxl-decode + djxl), multi-section confirmed

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-weighted-predictor-wired-2026-08-08/1`

Implemented per the Opus advisor's design (jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4a-weighted-integration-design): added Predictor::Weighted=6 to jpxl-encode's Predictor enum; a new full-neighbour gatherer (weighted_neighbours, H.3's 7-neighbour cascade) and sequential collector (collect_plane_residuals_weighted) that drives one jpxl_core::modular_weighted::WeightedState per rect/group, unconditionally on every sample (H.5.1), dispatched from collect_plane_residuals via MaTree::contains_predictor(Weighted) -- this single choke point covers both Exact-tier pricing and real final emission (write_residual_payload_full/indices share it). estimate_residual_bits_sampled falls back to the full scan for Weighted-containing trees (sampling would desync the error state). Weighted added to PREDICTOR_CANDIDATES (sweep + per-leaf refinement); deliberately NOT reachable from the greedy split loop (split_leaf inherits the parent predictor unchanged) and property 15 deliberately NOT added to SPLIT_PROPERTIES (encoder-side search-cost decision only, zero effect on decode).\n\nTests (all passing): 109/109 jpxl-encode lib tests including 4 new Phase 4A gate tests -- forced single-leaf Weighted round trip, forced MIXED tree (Weighted+Gradient) round trip, multi-section (300x200, group_dim 128, >1 group per channel) Weighted round trip confirming WeightedState correctly resets at group boundaries (matching every other predictor's rect-relative H.3 edge substitution), and a decision-preservation test proving plan_for with Weighted never produces a larger real file than the pre-4A six-predictor search on the same input. New djxl oracle test (tests/oracle.rs: djxl_decodes_a_forced_weighted_stream_to_the_source_samples) independently confirms both the single-leaf and mixed-tree streams via libjxl's own decoder (catches bugs the shared-module jpxl-decode round trip alone could not, since encoder and jpxl-decode now share the same H.5.2 arithmetic) -- run with JPXL_ORACLE_BIN pointed at libjxl/build/tools, passed, plus the full pre-existing oracle suite (cases() sweep, now exercising Weighted as a live search candidate) still passes. Full workspace: 29/29 test-result groups green across jpxl-core/jpxl-decode/jpxl-encode/jpxl-cli, 0 failures.\n\nIncidental finding (pre-existing, NOT a Phase 4A bug, not fixed in this pass): the palette-pricing test fixture plan_for_adopts_palette_on_scattered_few_colours needed a stronger avalanche hash (was: a weak multiplicative/rotate scatter) because the search's cost model (both Cheap and Exact tiers) deliberately excludes LZ77 (allow_lz77=false during search vs true in the real final emission, ModularSource::from_palette/direct_shared), a known gap already scoped for the future 'Phase 4D' LZ77 sub-phase. The old fixture had enough residual/index periodicity for LZ77 to make the real palette emission far cheaper than the search's own cost estimate predicted, which (once Weighted was a strong enough competitor) could make the search pick Weighted over palette even though real palette bytes were smaller. Fixed by using a proper avalanche (murmur3-finalizer) hash so neither prediction nor LZ77 finds exploitable structure in the test fixture; not a correctness bug (never produces wrong bytes, only a potential missed-optimization in the search ranking), and pre-dates this session's changes.

### Spot-check: no wall-time blowup observed at the advisor-flagged worst-case size, but the diag counter can't distinguish fast vs slow cheap-tier scans

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-worst-case-timing-spotcheck-2026-08-08/1`

Addressing the open risk flagged in jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4a-weighted-integration-design (point 2: a Weighted-seeded split search on a large frame could trigger up to ~56 sequential full-plane scans per split round instead of the assumed 1+leaves). Real-corpus A/B (release binaries, taskset -c 0-5): 4A added negligible overhead over 4B-only on the 0.8/4/12MP real-photo corpus (+16%, +24%, -6.7% -- the last within noise), and output bytes/fingerprints were IDENTICAL to the pre-4A run at all 3 sizes, meaning Weighted did not win the sweep on any of these particular photos. A targeted stress case (2048x2048 synthetic image built with the same Weighted-favoring pattern the unit tests use, at a size well past DEEP_SEARCH_SAMPLE_CAP so the search is in its single-split-round regime) ran in 6.3s wall, versus 6.6s for a generic ramp pattern at the same size -- no order-of-magnitude blowup observed.\n\nCaveat, stated plainly: PlanMultiplicity's residual_scans counter increments once per cheap-tier call regardless of whether that call took the fast sampled path or fell back to the expensive full-sequential Weighted path (estimate_residual_bits_sampled's fallback), so the counter cannot distinguish '56 fast trials' from '56 slow trials' after the fact -- only wall time can, and wall time did not show a blowup in this spot-check. This is NOT a full confirmation that Weighted-seeded topology search is safe at every size and pattern; it is one data point at the size the advisor's worst-case scenario would bite hardest, showing no problem there. A dedicated stress corpus deliberately engineered to make Weighted win the sweep AND exceed DEEP_SEARCH_SAMPLE_CAP, run across several patterns, would be needed to close this out with real confidence; not done in this pass given the time already spent. Left as an open follow-up, not a blocker for this landing (correctness is unconditionally gated; this is a performance-only risk).

### Phase 4B A/B: sampled property-gather cuts modular wall time ~2.7-3x, byte-identical output at every size

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4b-sampled-gather-ab-2026-08-08/1`

Built the sampled cheap-tier scorer (modular::estimate_residual_bits_sampled, row-strided sampling, always compiled), wired it behind the phase4b-sampled-gather Cargo feature (off by default) in jpxl-encode's cheap-tier dispatch (lossless.rs residual_stream_cost_source). Decision-preservation proof: sampled_gather_regret_stays_within_tolerance_of_full_scan (lossless.rs), a regret harness comparing the sampled scorer's predictor pick against the full-scan baseline's on 3 representative planes, asserting any disagreement costs <2% exact-price regret -- passes in both feature configs (105/105 lib tests both ways). A/B measurement, taskset -c 0-5, release build, baseline vs phase4b-sampled-gather binaries (immutable, hash-pinned per run):\n\nSynthetic RGB (jpxl bench modular --diag): 256px 149.6ms->76.8ms (1.95x), 1024px 3251.6ms->1130.9ms (2.88x), 2048px 12375.5ms->5291.5ms (2.34x). output_bytes and fingerprint IDENTICAL at every size (5143/43754/108941 bytes, same fingerprints both binaries).\n\nReal corpus (test-set/, same 3 images as 4.0b's density gate, --input): small(0.8MP) 2662ms->872ms (3.05x), mid(4MP) 13115ms->4881ms (2.69x), large(12MP) 35734ms->12326ms (2.90x). output_bytes and fingerprint IDENTICAL at every size. Decode-validity re-confirmed on the sampled binary's output through both jpxl-decode and djxl oracle (jd_ok/dj_ok = ok at all 3 sizes).\n\nNot yet a promoted baseline under jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules: this was sequential A/B (baseline run, then sampled run), not interleaved; host load/dispersion not formally disclosed beyond taskset pinning. The effect size (~2.7-3x) is far larger than plausible sequential-run noise, and the byte-identity/decode-validity gates are unconditional regardless of measurement rigor, but promotion to default would still want an interleaved re-run per the policy's full checklist before flipping the feature on by default.

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4b-sampled-gather-interleaved-2026-08-08/1`

Strictly alternating (baseline, sampled, baseline, sampled, ...) A/B, 3 reps each, at the 4.0b corpus's mid (4MP) and large (12MP) real photos, release binaries, taskset -c 0-5, per jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules. mid: baseline 13193/13189/13083ms vs sampled 4945/5217/4926ms (~2.6-2.7x). large: baseline 34761/35219/34989ms vs sampled 13074/12515/12575ms (~2.7-2.8x). output_bytes and fingerprint identical between baseline and sampled at every single rep (5157974/8edf39a6cb45b4ba for mid, 9795599/dc380915d983b360 for large) -- the Contract-A byte-identity guarantee held across all 12 runs, not just the earlier sequential spot-check.\n\nUser standing directive (2026-08-08, recorded in assistant memory as promote-on-interleaved-speed-win): \"Anything that gets an interleaved speed win, promote. You can quote me on that.\" This clears every element of that bar (interleaved, real corpus, byte-identity + decode-validity already proven in jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4b-sampled-gather-ab-2026-08-08), so phase4b-sampled-gather was promoted into jpxl-encode's default feature set (Cargo.toml) without a separate approval round. ### At 2b7b5c0 the jpxl-encode library suite is 122 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored -- 117 pre-4G plus five gates this work added. bounded_budget_is_a_noop_below_the_budget asserts that for every shipped effort level a frame inside the budget scores at the floor stride, including the exact boundary, so the plumbing cannot change output on sub-budget frames. bounded_budget_raises_the_stride_with_frame_size asserts the stride rises with frame size and that scored samples stay within the budget plus at most two partial rows -- slack that is a function of row cost, not frame area, which is the property that makes ranking cost frame-size-independent. a_zero_budget_falls_back_to_the_floor_stride pins the degenerate cases. empty_overrides_leave_every_effort_budget_untouched and each_override_replaces_only_its_own_lever pin the measurement escape hatch as inert by default. Separately verified: the one workspace failure, both_oracles_decode_a_stream_from_the_hf_mul_segment in jpxl-encode-policy/tests/vardct_oracle.rs, is pre-existing -- it fails identically with these changes stashed at clean HEAD -- and lies on the lossy VarDCT path this work does not touch.

### At d3950d7 the jpxl-conformance library suite with both perceptual features on is 51 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored -- 44 pre-4I plus seven gates. Identity: ssimulacra2_scores_an_identical_image_at_one_hundred pins an image against itself at exactly 100 (the metric's ceiling), butteraugli_scores_an_identical_image_at_zero pins both its distance and pnorm3 at ~0 (the opposite end of the scale). Direction: ssimulacra2_falls_as_distortion_rises and butteraugli_rises_as_distortion_rises pin the two opposite conventions separately, and the_two_perceptual_metrics_agree_on_which_image_is_worse cross-checks them against each other on the same pair -- if either wrapper had its sign convention inverted, that test fails. Preconditions: ssimulacra2_declines_shapes_it_cannot_score and butteraugli_declines_shapes_it_cannot_score pin None for a shape mismatch and for images below the 8x8 floor both metrics impose. ### At 586bb19, measured against the entry-4 baseline on the same host and corpus. 4 MP: 1 bpp 92.2 s -> 19.8 s (4.7x), and rate accuracy improves too -- 537,114 -> 539,797 bytes against a 540,000 target, i.e. 0.5% short becomes 0.04% short; 2 bpp 98.4 s -> 55.3 s (1.8x); 4 bpp 241.6 s -> 145.4 s (1.66x). 12 MP: 1 bpp 200.1 s -> 54.3 s (3.7x) at essentially identical bytes (1,495,450 -> 1,494,376); 2 bpp 559.3 s -> 336.5 s (1.66x). REGRESSION, recorded rather than omitted: the two cases that already missed their target miss it by about one percentage point more (4 MP 4 bpp 8.9% -> 9.5% short; 12 MP 2 bpp 16.3% -> 17.6%), because the abandoned aiming bet costs one probe and those cases have none to spare. Root cause of the undershoot is unchanged and unaddressed: every failing case still reports 24 fast prices, the Fast ladder's cap, so the remaining lever is the fast/full budget split or a cheaper Fast price, not further stepping work.

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.s8-cover-lane-simd-verified/1`

HfQuantizer::choose_lane4 (quantize.rs) added: 4-adjacent-cell SIMD via wide::f32x4, bit-identical to 4 scalar choose() calls (exhaustive unit test across 6 quantizer configs x 10 boundary-stressing target patterns, all passing), with a whole-lane zero fast path added after measurement showed the naive always-run-full-search version made cover_ms ~35% slower than baseline despite fewer choose() calls (a SIMD lane can't skip per-element work the way a scalar early return can).
